findings.evidence: “Situation, Behavior, Impact, then an open question” and “ask for one recent example and what it affected” restate familiar coaching knowledge. The 10-line delivery and 13-line receiving sections are largely activation rather than expert knowledge; the recognition stop rule also recurs in R1, delivery and follow-up.
findings.fix: Compress the standard SBI and receiving-feedback explanations into brief activation cues, retaining one worked example for each. State the recognition stop rule once rather than repeating it in routing, delivery and follow-up. Preserve the more distinctive thin-evidence, power, mediation and ownership decisions.

findings.evidence: “Use them for recognition and recaps, never for the first delivery of corrective feedback” categorically prohibits private written delivery without an escape hatch for accessibility needs, agreed communication preferences or asynchronous work.
findings.fix: Default to a private live conversation for first delivery of corrective feedback. Permit a short, factual private written opener when accessibility, agreed preferences or asynchronous constraints make it appropriate and policy permits it; apply the same confidentiality checks and offer a live follow-up.

findings.evidence: “Pre-send gate, on the final text of every draft: every sentence passes the dispute test” extends the record-based test at line 45 beyond factual assertions. The receiving and expectation-reset branches require questions, requests and future options, which cannot themselves be disputed by pointing to a historical record.
findings.fix: Apply the dispute test specifically to factual assertions, not every sentence. Explicitly allow open questions, requests, commitments and the speaker's clearly labeled reactions. Validate future options against stated estimates, assumptions and costs rather than requiring a historical record for them.

findings.evidence: The qualifying R5 conflict branch requires giving each person their own SBI feedback first, but its separate-conversation example opens “I've noticed tension between you and [colleague] around [topic].” It supplies an interpretation without a concrete situation, observable behavior or impact, contradicting the main skill's impression-only and SBI rules.
findings.fix: Replace the separate-conversation opener with each person's own observable instance and impact, followed by an open question: “In [review/date], your comment said [exact wording]. [Observed work impact]. How did you see that exchange?” If the facilitator lacks an instance, use a claim-free information-gathering question and explicitly distinguish that from delivering SBI feedback.
